steps.title: Read the brand page
steps.detail: Found a general claim that ingredients are ethically sourced.

steps.title: Followed the sourcing pages
steps.detail: Opened the brand's pages on how it buys ingredients.

steps.title: Looked ingredient by ingredient
steps.detail: Found specific sourcing stories and named suppliers for some ingredients.

steps.title: Searched for outside evidence
steps.detail: Looked for an independent scheme that covers the claim as written.

steps.title: Tested the words themselves
steps.detail: 'Ethically sourced' has no stated meaning or scope, so no source can confirm it as written.

headline: Vague
why: Evidence exists for some ingredients. The claim covers all ingredients and does not say what 'ethically sourced' means, so it cannot be tested as written.
what_it_means: The work behind the claim may be real. The wording is wider than the evidence.
what_would_help: Good news: the evidence is partly there. Name the ingredient, the supplier and the standard, and the claim becomes checkable.

evidence.name: Brand pages for individual ingredients
evidence.note: Specific evidence for some ingredients, not all.

evidence.name: Independent scheme covering all ingredients
evidence.note: No single scheme covers the claim as written.

next_action.label: Copy suggested rewrite
next_action.text: The [ingredient] in this product is bought directly from [named supplier or cooperative] in [country], under [named scheme or published standard].

team_check: Before the demo, copy the exact claim wording and page address from lush.com, and confirm which ingredient pages name suppliers.
summary: The words are wider than the evidence.
tip_short: Name the ingredient, the supplier and the standard.
takeaway: Ask the brand what it covers.
